events.flavourText: Big flowers, flogged at the market through a February of frost and sleet.

items.flavourText: Combination locks have the codes sealed inside the cases — only a safe-cracker can open them. Also rejects, also nicked.
Brakes don't work. Rodney almost crashed it on the test drive.
The 'priceless' statue is worth £17 on Portobello Road. Mr Ram doesn't exist.

items.displayName: Boxes of lead from a fallout shelter
items.flavourText: Originally meant for a DIY nuclear fallout shelter. Heavy, suspicious, hard to shift.
A bath tub of vile yellow liquid decanted into branded bottles in the lounge. Grandad stamps the boxes.
Nicked from Clapham Junction. Used for railway tunnel signs because it glows in the dark.
Tells the time in every capital city in the world — except London.
Rusted and broken — bought drunk down the One-Eleven Club. Scrap value about £20.
Cheap, naff, and you have to leg it the moment you see Old Bill.
Industrial models, all 'guaranteed — sort of — to be in perfect working order'.
Poached from a private estate, with bribes to a corrupt gamekeeper. Plus an axe murderer's loose in the area.
Flogged in cold weather. Eventually has to be knocked out to cover Albert's stunt-man losses.
Each doll has a different voice chip meant for another toy entirely.
Crackle, drop calls, generally useless. Still trying to flog them in the Nag's Head.
Retails at £375 'normally'. Comes with a free plug-in telephone if you'll just take it.
BBC Masters in third-party Viglen cases with a stick-on badge. Flogged one to a vicar.

items.displayName: Lusty Linda & Erotic Estelle inflatable dolls
items.flavourText: Filled with explosive propane gas due to a factory mix-up. Self-inflate. Will detonate if heated.
Continental current only. Won't run on British power without a transformer the size of a suitcase.
Definitely not from Jersey. Trigger says they taste off.
Arnie fakes a heart attack mid-deal and escapes in a fake ambulance.
Big flowers, flogged at the market through a February of frost and sleet.
Bring trouble with the Driscoll Brothers in the next episode.
Catch fire. One fitted in the Jolly Boys' coach blew up near Margate.
Dodgy enough that he had to lay low and skip the country.
It's tap water. Bottling plant is the lounge. Possibly contaminated.
Thought he was buying ladies' wigs to flog to old dears in the Nag's Head. They are very much not.
Aimed at the trendy market. Rodney unwillingly becomes the model.
Sold from the back of the Reliant. Tin says it all.

items.displayName: DIY North Sea gas conversion kits
items.flavourText: Sent Rodney with chickenpox to flog them on the Mountbatten Estate. Which is all-electric.

items.displayName: China cats playing 'How Much Is That Doggy in the Window'
items.flavourText: A balls-up at the factory put the wrong chimes in. Cats playing a song about a dog.
Sing a full repertoire of Chinese lullabies.
Play 36 different national anthems on the hour. Loudly.
Fling the discs out like clay pigeons.
Are actually paint strippers.
Hit the health market. They do not cure anything.
